overview: Black pins the f3 knight at once with ...Bg4 after 1...d6, aiming at an early exchange and a solid Old Indian-style set-up. White usually plays 3.e4 or 3.c4 and, after ...Bxf3, takes the bishop pair and a space edge. Black gets a sound but passive position with doubled pawns possible, so the line is rare among strong players.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with e4 and c4 and use the bishop pair after ...Bxf3.
Play e3 and Be2, aiming for a London-style game, or h3 to force a decision.

black_ideas.idea: Pin the knight and exchange on f3 to cut White's central influence.
Build an Old Indian set-up with ...Nd7, ...e5 or ...e6 and ...Nf6.

typical_structures.structure: White centre d4/e4 against Black d6/e6 or e5 with the dark-squared bishop kept.

character.notes: Solid Old Indian-style set-up, but Black ends up cramped with few active ideas.

soundness.notes: Playable, but gives White an easy edge; not refuted.

structure.notes: Fluid centre, White's e4 or c4 and Black's d6; tension unresolved.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose 1...d6 and 2...Bg4 against 1.d4.

level.notes: Simple plan but not a good first repertoire.

character.reason: Black's compact set-up is hard to break down but passive.

level.reason: Simple ideas but not a first choice.

plans.reason: White gets the bishops and the centre.
